features.description: Parse urn:ankusa:claim:v1:<tenant>:<claim_id> into tenant_id, claim_id, and the /v1/claims/{tenant_id}/{claim_id} path; anything else raises InvalidClaimRefError.
GET /v1/claims/{tenant_id}/{claim_id} and return the body bytes verbatim (text, binary, empty).
A malformed ref, or a sha256 that isn't 64 lowercase hex chars, raises InvalidClaimRefError before any request is made.
Returned bytes are verified against the expected sha256; a mismatch raises ClaimIntegrityError.
404 -> ClaimNotFoundError; other 4xx -> ClaimRejectedError(status, body); 5xx, any other non-200, an unfollowed redirect, or no connection -> ClaimCheckUnavailableError (retryable).
GET /health returns the JSON body on 200; anything else raises ClaimCheckUnavailableError.
Client-level headers ride on every request.
A per-client request timeout; exceeding it raises ClaimCheckUnavailableError.
An injectable transport (Python transport=, TypeScript fetch) replaces the network.
Parse x-ankusa-id/-source/-seq/-tenant and content-type case-insensitively; a missing or empty x-ankusa-id raises MissingHookIdError; seq is an integer only when it is all ASCII digits.
Create, list, read, replace, update, and delete route definitions over the route-management listener (routes.admin.port).
Get and replace the global IP rules.
Dry-run a request against the route table and return the decision without capturing anything.

2xx is success. 404 -> RouteNotFoundError; every other 4xx -> RoutesRejectedError(status, code = the body's error, field, message, conflicting_id, max_routes). Anything else that isn't 2xx (5xx, an unfollowed 3xx redirect, 1xx), a transport failure, or a non-JSON success body -> RoutesUnavailableError (retryable).

Route ids are checked before any request and then percent-encoded as one path segment: an id that isn't a string, is empty, or is exactly `.` or `..` raises InvalidRouteIdError (no request), while every other id travels with `/`, `?`, `#`, `%` and space escaped as %2F %3F %23 %25 %20.
Requests match the documented API: JSON bodies carry exactly the caller's input, and query parameters go out in input order with booleans as `true`/`false`.
GET /health on the route-management listener returns {status, routes}.
Operator API: health, Prometheus metrics, redacted config, DLQ list/replay, and quarantine.

2xx is success. A 409 whose body has error role_not_enabled -> RoleNotEnabledError(role); every other 4xx -> AdminRejectedError(status, code = the body's error). Anything else that isn't 2xx (5xx, an unfollowed 3xx redirect, 1xx) or a transport failure -> AdminUnavailableError (retryable).
